summary: A legal string of one-character words separated by single spaces contributes every character to the normalized output, so exact reversal requires Omega(n) work. Split, reverse, and join match that bound.

optimality.argument: Consider a valid length-n string made of one-character words separated by single spaces. Changing any word character changes the required reversed output, and the output itself has length n. A correct transformation therefore needs Omega(n) inspection and construction work. Python's split, reversed iteration, and join each process only a linear total number of characters, giving O(n) time.

replacement_checks.evidence: Every word character in a single-spaced one-character-word input appears in the result, and the normalized result has linear length.
Word extraction and output joining each inspect or copy a linear number of input or output characters.

The source-fidelity-verified examples cover ordinary spacing, leading and trailing spaces, and repeated internal spaces; black-box real-test execution verifies every existing ordinary check without inspecting its definition.
